system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: MFN
Title: Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer
Kind: direction
Summary: MFN in our favour is welcome; an MFN that obliges us to give the Vendor best terms is not.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No MFN obligation on Customer (MFN pricing in Customer's favour is welcome).
Position — fallback:
MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.
Position — walk-away:
Open-ended obligation to extend to Vendor any better terms given to any third party.
Detection guidance:
Identify who benefits from the MFN. Flag only when Customer must offer Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to others, or must match third-party offers. If the Vendor grants Customer best pricing, mark compliant and do not redline.

Redline guidance:
Delete the obligation on Customer; keep any Vendor-granted MFN.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.",
  "The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.",
  "The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs."
]

input.rationale: There is no pricing MFN anywhere in the Agreement (Articles V-VIII contain only the tiered per-trade fee table, and the Revisions clause at p0094 favours us). content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Result: deviation (MFN), preferred position taken.**

- No pricing MFN exists in the fee architecture (Articles V–VIII are a tiered per-trade table; the Revisions clause at p0094 runs in our favour and was not flagged).
- The responsive burden is Article XXII (p0139–p0141): we must notify Licensor of any bona fide third-party offer to buy our assets or merge, and Licensor gets five business days to take that offer — a most-favoured-offer/right-to-match mechanic on the Customer, which the playbook routes to MFN.
- It fails all three fallback elements (no defined product, whole term rather than 12 months, no like-for-like carve-out), so the redline removes the Customer-side obligation and conforms the two follow-on sentences so that "Right of First Refusal" and "Exercise Period" are not left dangling.

Minimality defect: revise only the words needed for one complete checklist level and remove extra terms.

Verifier reasons:
- Preferred level is complete: the operative text extinguishes the Licensee-side notice/most-favoured-offer and matching mechanic, which is the single preferred element. The finding is correctly classified as a deviation at the fallback level (no defined product, term-long duration, no like-for-like carve-out).
- Minimality defect 1 — scope creep in the conforming sentence: replace "Without notice to or the consent of the Licensor, the Licensee shall have the right to consummate any transaction with a third party" with either straight deletion of the sentence or a narrow conforming version (e.g. "The Licensee may consummate the transaction with the third party."). Striking "or the consent of the Licensor" is required: the deleted Article XXII never conditioned any transaction on Licensor consent, so the new words create a fresh, unnecessary consent-free permission covering all third-party transactions.
- Minimality defect 2 — surplus negative covenant: the added tail "and no other right to be notified of or to receive any terms that the Licensee offers to or receives from a third party" goes beyond removing the obligation and is unnecessary once the mechanic and its defined terms ("Right of First Refusal", "Exercise Period") are deleted. A simple deletion of the Article, or a one-line "Intentionally omitted / Licensor shall have no right of first refusal or right to match", achieves the element without new operative breadth.
- Intent risk to police before sending: the broadened "without ... the consent of the Licensor ... any transaction with a third party" language could contradict any retained assignment or change-of-control consent provision elsewhere in the Agreement (an effective override of that clause). Confirm the assignment article and, if a consent requirement is retained, narrow this sentence so the two do not conflict. Aside from this risk, no dangling defined terms or cross-references remain, since "Right of First Refusal" and "Exercise Period" were defined only in the deleted text.
- Margin comment is accurate and appropriately scoped; no separate flagging of the same term under ASSIGN should occur unless the assignment rule is independently breached.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.",
  "The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.",
  "A paid-up licence is perpetual.",
  "A paid-up licence is irrevocable.",
  "A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.",
  "The licence is transferable to Customer's successors."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.",
  "The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction."
]

Planner evidence and hints:

Before drafting an actionable proposal, call lookup_precedent. Treat returned approved language as an element-marked template, adapt it to this contract, and verify every marker; do not copy non-element extras.

Investigate every responsive location, choose one target level, validate the smallest complete proposal, map every target element, and submit one finding.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.",
  "Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.",
  "The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.",
  "The Services warranty lasts 90 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund.",
  "Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.",
  "Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.",
  "Services are warranted for at least 30 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund."
]

input.quote: ARTICLE XXII RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL During the term of this Agreement, the Licensor shall have the right (the "Right of First Refusal"), for a period (the "Exercise Period") expiring at 11:59 PM (Eastern Time) on the fifth (5th) business day after the giving of written notice by the Licensee that it has received a bonafide offer from a third party to (ii) purchase all or substantially all of the assets of Licensee
input.rationale: No pricing MFN exists in the Agreement (Articles V-VIII are only the tiered per-trade fee table, and the Revisions clause at p0094 runs in our favour). Article XXII, however, imposes a most-favoured-offer/right-to-match mechanic on us: we must notify Licensor of any bona fide third-party offer for our assets or a merger and give Licensor five business days to take that offer. The playbook assesses right-to-match and most-favoured-offer mechanics under MFN, and this one fails every fallback element - it is not confined to a defined product, it runs for the whole term (36 months plus a possible seven-year renewal at Licensor's option), and it has no like-for-like comparison carve-out. We therefore take the preferred position: the operative grant is replaced with a one-line no-first-refusal/no-match statement, and the follow-on sentence is restated so it carries its own antecedent for the transaction and the third party and remains expressly subject to the retained Change Of Control (p0134) and Assignment (p0149) consent provisions, so nothing dangles or contradicts.

proposal.summary: Negate the Article XXII first-refusal/matching mechanic and restate the follow-on sentence with its own antecedent, subordinated to the retained Change of Control and Assignment sections.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We removed the Article XXII obligation to notify Licensor of third-party offers and let Licensor take them, as our playbook does not accept a most-favoured-offer or matching right in the Vendor's favour, and we restated the follow-on sentence so it carries its own antecedent and remains subject to the retained Change Of Control and Assignment sections.

After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. MFN limited to a defined product, for 12 months, with reasonable-comparison carve-outs.

input.quote: ARTICLE XXII RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL During the term of this Agreement, the Licensor shall have the right (the \"Right of First Refusal\"), for a period (the \"Exercise Period\") expiring at 11:59 PM (Eastern Time) on the fifth (5th) business day after the giving of written notice by the Licensee that it has received a bonafide offer from a third party to (ii) purchase all or substantially all of the assets of Licensee
input.rationale: There is no pricing MFN anywhere in the Agreement (Articles V-VIII contain only the tiered per-trade fee table, and the Revisions clause at p0094 favours us). However, Article XXII imposes a most-favoured-offer/right-to-match mechanic on us: we must disclose any bona fide third-party offer for our assets or a merger and give Licensor five business days to take that offer on those terms. Under the playbook, a right-to-match or most-favoured-offer mechanic is assessed under MFN. It fails every fallback element - it is not confined to a defined product, it runs for the entire term (36 months plus a potential seven-year renewal at Licensor's option), and it has no like-for-like comparison carve-out - so we take the preferred position and remove the Customer-side obligation, conforming the two follow-on sentences that operated off the deleted mechanic so no dangling defined terms remain.

content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Result: deviation (MFN), preferred position taken.**

- No pricing MFN exists in the fee architecture (Articles V–VIII are a tiered per-trade table; the Revisions clause at p0094 runs in our favour and was not flagged).
- The responsive burden is Article XXII (p0139–p0141): we must notify Licensor of any bona fide third-party offer to buy our assets or merge, and Licensor gets five business days to take that offer — a most-favoured-offer/right-to-match mechanic on the Customer, which the playbook routes to MFN.
- It fails all three fallback elements (no defined product, whole term rather than 12 months, no like-for-like carve-out), so the redline removes the Customer-side obligation and conforms the two follow-on sentences so that "Right of First Refusal" and "Exercise Period" are not left dangling.

messages.content:
Independent verifier feedback follows. Exact unmet checklist text must be repaired in operative language:
Minimality defect: revise only the words needed for one complete checklist level and remove extra terms.

Verifier reasons:
- Preferred level is complete: the operative text extinguishes the Licensee-side notice/most-favoured-offer and matching mechanic, which is the single preferred element. The finding is correctly classified as a deviation at the fallback level (no defined product, term-long duration, no like-for-like carve-out).
- Minimality defect 1 — scope creep in the conforming sentence: replace "Without notice to or the consent of the Licensor, the Licensee shall have the right to consummate any transaction with a third party" with either straight deletion of the sentence or a narrow conforming version (e.g. "The Licensee may consummate the transaction with the third party."). Striking "or the consent of the Licensor" is required: the deleted Article XXII never conditioned any transaction on Licensor consent, so the new words create a fresh, unnecessary consent-free permission covering all third-party transactions.
- Minimality defect 2 — surplus negative covenant: the added tail "and no other right to be notified of or to receive any terms that the Licensee offers to or receives from a third party" goes beyond removing the obligation and is unnecessary once the mechanic and its defined terms ("Right of First Refusal", "Exercise Period") are deleted. A simple deletion of the Article, or a one-line "Intentionally omitted / Licensor shall have no right of first refusal or right to match", achieves the element without new operative breadth.
- Intent risk to police before sending: the broadened "without ... the consent of the Licensor ... any transaction with a third party" language could contradict any retained assignment or change-of-control consent provision elsewhere in the Agreement (an effective override of that clause). Confirm the assignment article and, if a consent requirement is retained, narrow this sentence so the two do not conflict. Aside from this risk, no dangling defined terms or cross-references remain, since "Right of First Refusal" and "Exercise Period" were defined only in the deleted text.
- Margin comment is accurate and appropriately scoped; no separate flagging of the same term under ASSIGN should occur unless the assignment rule is independently breached.

Independent verifier feedback follows. Exact unmet checklist text must be repaired in operative language:
Intent defect: restore unrelated commercial language and remove contradictions introduced by the redline.

Verifier reasons:
- Preferred level is complete: the operative grant of the Right of First Refusal/matching mechanic against Licensee is replaced with an express negation, so Customer carries no most-favoured-offer obligation benefiting Vendor.
- Minimality is acceptable: only the Article XXII grant and the conditional opening of the follow-on sentence were touched; the one-line negation is a concise substitute for the deleted mechanic and adds no requirement outside the MFN checklist ("or right to match" merely restates the same deleted mechanic).
- Intent fails on dangling antecedents. The retained sentence now reads "The Licensee shall have the right to consummate the transaction with the third party," but "the transaction" and "the third party" were introduced only in the deleted first paragraph (the bona fide third-party offer to purchase assets or merge). Repair by either deleting the follow-on sentence together with the grant, or restating it with its own antecedent, e.g. "Licensee may consummate any sale of all or substantially all of its assets, or any merger or consolidation, with a third party without any notice to, or first-refusal or matching right of, Licensor."
- Intent also fails on a contradictory retained sentence. Stripped of its condition ("In the event the Licensor declines or fails to exercise... the Right of First Refusal"), the retained sentence reads as an unconditional Licensee right to consummate a third-party transaction, which conflicts with the retained Change of Control provision (p0134) and assignment provision (p0149) that still require Licensor consent. Add an express subordination (e.g. "subject to Article [Change of Control] and Article [Assignment]") or delete the sentence entirely.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.",
  "Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.",
  "The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.",
  "The Services warranty lasts 90 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund.",
  "Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.",
  "Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.",
  "Services are warranted for at least 30 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund."
]

elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Article III is untouched: "Licensee acknowledges that Licensor owns all right, title, and interest in and to the Licensed Technology and all Intellectual Property Rights therein," and customization work is a Derivative Work of the Platform Software; the insertion grants only a licence, not ownership, of the Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment language anywhere; the operative insertion says only "Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence."

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Article III retained in full: Licensor owns all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology (Licensed Know-How plus Licensed Software) and all Intellectual Property Rights therein.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual ... licence to use, modify and sublicense ... any customization or development work performed for Licensee under this Section (the 'Deliverables')," and the Notwithstanding overrides Article XXI's automatic licence termination; the grant covers the Deliverables including Licensor IP within them.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Insertion reads "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence," notwithstanding Articles II, III, VI and XXI.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Express "royalty-free" in the granting sentence.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The insertion only limits Licensor's use ("Any licence or right of Licensor in data ... is limited to processing such data solely to provide the services"); no affirmative sentence stating Licensee retains all right, title and interest in data belonging to, supplied by or processed for it.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: "Any licence or right of Licensor in data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee is limited to processing such data solely to provide the services under this Agreement." No retained resale/independent-exploitation right in Licensee data appears in the cited text.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No joint-ownership language exists in the retained or inserted text; Article III vests sole ownership of Licensed Technology in Licensor, and the insertion creates only a licence, so the condition (delete joint ownership) does not arise.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Article III preserved unamended: Licensor owns all right, title and interest in the Licensed Technology (defined as Licensed Know-How and Licensed Software) and all Intellectual Property Rights therein.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: "Notwithstanding Articles II, III, VI and XXI, Licensor grants Licensee a perpetual ... licence ..."; the XXI override neutralises the automatic licence termination on expiry/termination.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Express "irrevocable" in the inserted grant.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Express "worldwide" in the inserted grant; no Field-of-Use or territory qualifier is applied to the Deliverables licence because the grant overrides Article II.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Express "royalty-free" in the inserted grant.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "licence to use, modify and sublicense for Licensee's business any customization or development work performed for Licensee under this Section"; the Notwithstanding Article II override displaces the II(g) no-modification-without-consent restriction as to Deliverables.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: "use, modify and sublicense for Licensee's business"; the override of Articles II and VI displaces the II(c) sublicense/transfer prohibition as to the Deliverables.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Second inserted sentence covers every category — "data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Licensee" — and confines Licensor to "processing such data solely to provide the services under this Agreement."

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single inserted grant supplies all four licence modifiers (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free), the use/modify and sublicense rights for Licensee's business, and the data-use limitation, while Article III leaves Licensor's ownership of its platform and know-how intact.

Preferred level is not reached: there is no Customer ownership of, or Vendor assignment of, the customization Deliverables, and no affirmative sentence that Licensee retains all rights in its data. To reach preferred the drafter would need an operative 'Licensor hereby assigns to Licensee all right, title and interest in the Deliverables' sentence plus a 'Licensee retains all right, title and interest in Licensee data' sentence.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion at the customization clause, no deletions, no survival tails, expense, indemnity or procedural extras. The Notwithstanding reference to Articles II, III, VI and XXI is not gratuitous boilerplate here — without it the retained II(c) sublicense ban, II(g) modification ban, Article III ownership/copy restriction and Article XXI automatic licence termination would each directly contradict the new grant and render the licence internally inconsistent.

Intent is preserved: the Field-of-Use limit, copy and notice restrictions, infringement-reporting duty and Article XXI return obligations continue to govern the Licensed Technology; the override is scoped to the Deliverables licence only, leaving no dangling term or undefined trigger ('Deliverables' is defined in the inserted text).

Minor residual to flag in the rationale only: Article XXI(b) still requires return of all Licensed Technology within five days, which sits awkwardly with a perpetual Deliverables licence if the Deliverables are treated as Derivative Works — a short carve-out ('other than the Deliverables licensed under Section VII(b)') would tidy this, but it is not required by any selected element.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).

Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.

Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Licensor may request such an audit no more than once in any 12-month period" — replaces the original unlimited request right and caps frequency.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "on at least 30 days' prior written notice to Licensee"; the original sentence giving Licensee 30 days to permit an audit after a request (a compliance deadline, not advance notice) was replaced, so no contradictory timing survives.

elements.evidence: Inserted: "Each such audit shall be conducted during Licensee's normal business hours".

elements.evidence: "no more than once in any 12-month period" satisfies a once-per-year cap.

elements.evidence: "at least 30 days' prior written notice" exceeds the 15-day fallback minimum.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Not a fallback element; noted only for completeness — retained 5% threshold satisfies the preferred cost element.

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: MINCOMMIT
Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer
Kind: presence
Summary: We do not take-or-pay without an exit.
Severity: medium
Category: commercial
Position — preferred:
No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.
Position — fallback:
Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.
Position — walk-away:
Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.
Detection guidance:
"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.
Redline guidance:
Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.",
  "Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services."
]
