You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use document tools to inspect every responsive clause, definition, and cross-reference; do not stop at the first hit.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and never flag an obligation that benefits our party.

Keep rule boundaries precise. A sourcing requirement that applies only when Customer voluntarily uses Vendor's interface is not exclusivity when Customer is expressly free to use alternatives. A disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic belongs under MFN and is not also exclusivity unless it outright prohibits using alternatives after the mechanic is honoured. Natural-term non-renewal belongs under RENEWAL and is not Vendor mid-term termination for convenience under T4C; do not flag the same term twice. An unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right even if the clause does not use the word "convenience". An auto-renewal clause that either party may terminate on notice does not establish that Vendor termination is term-end-only unless the effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. Under IP, inspect every Customer Data licence: distribution, resale, independent exploitation, or use for the broader "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" is not cured by adding a separate ownership sentence and must be narrowed expressly to processing solely to provide the Services. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer is service delivery, not independent exploitation. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not a standing Vendor licence; do not flag that hypothetical consent alone.

Do not weaken Customer while completing an element. A Customer licence-transfer right does not justify expanding a mutual assignment exception for Vendor; draft a Customer-only licence transfer. A conditional insurance element covering Customer Data must reach every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer; do not narrow it to a few named examples. When inserting qualifiers into an existing clause, keep every untouched word verbatim rather than cosmetically rewriting the whole sentence.

Resolve assignment and licence scope literally. For ASSIGN fallback, "other assignments require consent" means every non-successor assignment: a retained no-consent affiliate exception conflicts with that level, even when mutual. For LICENSE, first resolve whether the defined Customer already includes affiliates; do not add duplicate coverage. A licence grant to an entity ordinarily reaches that entity's authorized personnel, so do not rewrite a separate personnel/access clause unless it expressly prohibits use needed by the new grant. Express a permitted licence transfer directly (for example, "without Vendor's approval"); do not add a broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause.

The preferred and fallback positions are operative checklists, not drafting themes. First classify under the supplied playbook semantics. If the existing bargain meets every fallback element on its material terms, submit compliant and do not upgrade it merely to reach preferred wording. If it genuinely fails fallback, choose a preferred or fallback target and make the shortest operative change that meets every element at that target level.

For every deviation or missing proposal, map each target element exactly once in elementCoverage. Before drafting, search for each element independently. Use already_met only with a verbatim document quote, cite that quote's paragraph in paragraphIds, and do not restate an already-met element in a new operation. Use addressed_by_operation with one-based operationIndexes. You may leave an element unaddressed only by submitting needs_review with a concrete explanation. Never claim that a margin comment cures missing operative language.

Draft surgically: replace only the existing words or sentence that need to change, group related elements into one operation, and preserve unrelated text. When curing a prohibition, edit the prohibitory operator and duration or use one short affirmative permission; do not both negate the restriction and recite every permitted activity. Avoid a broad "notwithstanding" override when a precise conforming edit can resolve the conflict. After rendering, inspect every retained reference to a term or sentence you changed: an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained mechanic is an intent failure. Prefer a fallback edit when deleting to preferred would require collateral rewrites. A replace may add at most 1.5 times as many words as it removes. For a genuinely absent clause, use insert_after and draft the shortest clause that carries only the still-missing target elements; do not rewrite a neighbouring clause.

The atomic checklist is the ceiling as well as the floor. Model language and precedents are source material, not permission to add non-element boilerplate. Omit survival tails, at-own-expense language, incidental or special damages, procedures, and other ancillary terms unless a selected element requires them. Meet numeric floors and ceilings at the selected threshold; do not volunteer a more onerous duration or amount just because it appears at the other level. Preserve exact nouns, temporal anchors, and bases: "fees paid or payable" may not become broader "all amounts paid or payable", and "preceding the claim" is not interchangeable with "preceding the event giving rise to the claim." Preserve every word in a mixed phrase that the target does not require changing: for example, curing "without reduction or termination rights" must not silently remove the reduction restriction. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief does not defeat an otherwise exclusive merits forum. A preferred "no non-compete or field-of-use restriction" is not met while Vendor retains an exclusive right that prevents Customer from using or licensing its own product or brand. Do not add terms that are absent from the selected checklist.

For a preferred no-liquidated-damages result, make the prohibition unconditional and conform every retained formula, instalment, or "if any" payment mechanic; otherwise use the exact fallback cap instead. Defining a payment as zero while retaining machinery that contemplates it is not a clean cure.

For T4C, do not add "in whole or in part" or a partial-termination right unless the selected element and this contract's Order Form structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the selected assistance duration must be available after every covered expiry or termination; a pre-expiry request condition does not establish a post-termination duration. State that certified deletion occurs after data return, not merely after assistance. For WARRANTY fallback, a report or output conforming to a user manual is not a software-to-documentation warranty unless that report is itself the defined software deliverable; add the shortest express software conformance warranty when needed.

For a preferred liability cap, verify the definition behind every payment-carve-out noun. A carve-out limited to a narrowly defined "Fees" category does not exclude all Customer payment obligations; surgically use "amounts due" or equally comprehensive operative language. Do not add explanatory examples such as "including subscription fees" to the cap formula when lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms is sufficient.

Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Finding quotes must be 600 characters or fewer. Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and accurately explain the operative change.

For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding. For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent 551 FX IB Associates, LLC (Licensee); counterparty is SFG Financial Corp, a/k/a E-Path FX (Licensor).

Rule and atomic checklists:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Preferred atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.",
  "Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.",
  "The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.",
  "The Services warranty lasts 90 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund.",
  "Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.",
  "Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code."
]

Fallback atomic elements (copy the JSON string values exactly):
[
  "Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.",
  "Services are warranted for at least 30 days.",
  "Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.",
  "Warranty remedies include a refund."
]

input.comment: [Playbook] Article VIX currently provides the Licensed Technology "AS IS" with all express and implied warranties disclaimed, which is our walk-away position, so we added a short express warranty at our fallback level: 90 days conformance to Documentation for the Licensed Software, 30 days for the support services, with repair or replacement or a refund of fees paid. We also carved that warranty out of the two disclaimer sentences so it is not swallowed.

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (WARRANTY).**

- **What the document says:** Article VIX is a pure disclaimer — the Licensed Technology is provided "AS IS" with *all* warranties, express or implied, disclaimed, and Licensor expressly does not warrant that Errors or "NONCONFORMITY TO ITS DOCUMENTATION CAN OR WILL BE CORRECTED." No affirmative warranty exists elsewhere; Article VII(f)'s "commercially reasonable efforts to provide Error Corrections" is a service obligation (and is further cut back by VII(h)), not a warranty, and carries no repair/replace or refund remedy. This is the playbook's walk-away position.
- **Target level chosen:** fallback (shortest complete cure).
- **Redline (validated, ok:true, 3 ops):**
  1. Lead-in carve-out in the "AS IS" sentence (p0110);
  2. Same carve-out before the "does not warrant" sentence (p0113), so the retained no-correction language no longer contradicts the new warranty;
  3. One short inserted warranty after p0116: 90 days conformance of the Licensed Software to its Documentation, 30 days professional-and-workmanlike Technical Support Services, remedy of repair or replacement or refund of fees paid.
- Kept to fallback only — no 12-month period, compliance-with-laws or malicious-code warranties, and no ancillary procedure or survival language.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed customer-side contract redline in a fresh context.
Treat the preferred and fallback positions as separate atomic checklists. Evaluate the operative rendered language, not the drafter's confidence or margin comment. Copy every supplied element string exactly into the corresponding output item, assess both levels, and return met, not_met, or cannot_tell with concise textual evidence. A conditional element is met when its stated condition does not apply, but explain why.

Apply rule boundaries: voluntary use of one Vendor interface is not a sole-supplier promise when Customer remains free to use alternatives; a disclosure, right-to-match, or most-favoured offer mechanic is MFN rather than exclusivity unless alternatives remain prohibited after compliance; natural-term non-renewal is evaluated under RENEWAL, not as mid-term T4C; an unconditional Customer election to terminate is a convenience right. An auto-renewal clause permitting either party to terminate on notice does not make Vendor termination term-end-only unless the termination effective date is expressly tied to the end of the then-current term. A broad Vendor right to distribute, resell, independently exploit Customer Data, or use it for the wider "purposes contemplated by this Agreement" defeats the solely-to-provide-the-Services element even if ownership nominally remains with Customer. Processing to provide, secure, support, or improve the Services for Customer remains service delivery. A prohibition on another use unless Customer later gives express written consent is not itself a standing Vendor licence.

Fail intent if a Customer-only successor or licence-transfer element is implemented by granting Vendor a new assignment exception. A Customer Data insurance trigger must cover every category of data belonging to, supplied by, or processed for Customer, not merely selected named data types. Cosmetic deletion or paraphrase of words outside the target elements fails minimality.

For ASSIGN fallback, any retained no-consent non-successor exception—including a mutual affiliate exception—defeats "Other assignments require consent." Under LICENSE, resolve whether Customer already includes affiliates and fail minimality for duplicate coverage. A grant to an affiliate ordinarily permits use through its authorized personnel; a separate personnel/access edit is unnecessary unless retained language expressly contradicts the new grant. A broad notwithstanding override of the assignment clause is non-minimal when a direct "without Vendor approval" transfer permission will do.

The redline is position-complete when every element at either the preferred level or the fallback level is met. Do not mark a level complete if an element is omitted, merely promised in the comment, internally inconsistent, or depends on an undefined trigger. Deterministic regexes are evidence; inspect their result in substance as well as mechanically.

Minimal means the proposal changes only what is needed to reach one complete level, retains favourable existing language, avoids duplicating operative terms, and adds no requirement outside the chosen checklist. Treat model-language extras as extras: survival tails, at-own-expense language, additional damages categories, procedures, or boilerplate fail minimality unless a selected element requires them. For a missing clause, a concise insertion can be minimal even though all its words are new. Preserves intent means unrelated allocation, timing, remedies, references, and commercial mechanics survive without contradiction; fail intent if an edit leaves an undefined term, dangling cross-reference, or contradictory retained sentence.

Read nouns, modifiers, temporal anchors, amounts, bases, scope, and party direction literally. Do not infer "pro rata" merely from a refund that covers a post-termination period. Do not equate broader "all amounts paid or payable" with "fees paid or payable", "the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to a claim" with "the 12 months preceding the claim", or a deadline running from a request with one running from termination. A customary other-court carve-out solely for temporary injunctive relief preserves an otherwise exclusive merits forum; a broader alternate forum does not. A "no field-of-use restriction" result is not complete while an exclusive Vendor right prevents Customer use of its own product or brand. Fail minimality when a fallback proposal exceeds its numeric threshold without necessity. A no-liquidated-damages result must be unconditional and leave no retained formula, instalment, or contingent payment mechanic. Treat removal of any word outside the chosen elements—even a Customer-favourable restriction—as a minimality failure. Do not infer an omitted element from general commercial context.

For a liability cap, resolve the definition used by any Customer-payment carve-out. Language excluding only a narrowly defined subset of Fees does not cover Customer payment obligations as a whole. Treat explanatory examples added to an otherwise complete formula as non-minimal.

For T4C, treat "in whole or in part" as surplus unless the selected checklist and an actual Order Form or partial-termination structure require it.

For TRANSITION, the stated assistance period must apply after every covered expiry or termination; a request condition tied only to anticipated expiry does not suffice. Certified deletion must occur after data return. For WARRANTY fallback, do not treat reports, outputs, or services as software merely because they conform to a manual; require an express software-to-documentation warranty unless the contract defines the item as software.

Give actionable reasons. If an element is not met, name the exact defect the drafter must repair in operative language.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

You are in-house counsel producing a concise Markdown issues memo from verified findings.
Include: Executive summary; a Markdown table of findings with severity, rule, status and section; Walk-away items; Next steps.
Never invent a section reference or legal conclusion. Use only supplied findings.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Document: ARTICLE I CERTAIN DEFINITIONS For the purposes of this Agreement:

Findings:
[{"id":"f-indemn-52117ca5","ruleId":"INDEMN","ruleTitle":"Indemnification by Vendor","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION","rationale":"Article XII is a one-way Licensee indemnity in the Licensor's favour, and there is no Licensor indemnity anywhere in the Agreement; Article XIII goes further and states that \"UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE\" for third-party infringement claims arising from use of the Licensed Technology. That is walk-away territory under this rule (no Vendor IP indemnity at all, one-way Customer indemnity). We therefore added a Licensor IP indemnity at the fallback level - customary Licensee modification, combination and specification exclusions, procure/modify/replace and refund remedies, and a super-cap of three times annual fees - and conformed the Article XIII infringement disclaimer and liability cap so the new indemnity is not negated. We left the existing Licensee indemnity in place rather than pursuing the preferred position, which would require broader collateral rewrites.","proposal":"Add Licensor IP indemnity with customary exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies and a 3x annual fees super-cap, and conform Article XIII so it does not negate that indemnity.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-a16c518b","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:","rationale":"Licensor owns all Licensed Technology and Intellectual Property Rights (Article III), and enhancements/customization work we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) fall within that ownership as Derivative Works of the Platform Software. Our only rights are a non-exclusive, Field-of-Use licence that we may not modify (Article II(g)) or sublicense/transfer (Article II(c), Article VI) and that terminates with the Agreement (Article XXI). That fails the IP fallback: we have no perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense Deliverables for our business, and there is no limitation on Licensor's use of data we supply or that it processes for us. Licensor's retention of ownership in its own platform and know-how is acceptable and is preserved. We therefore propose the shortest fallback fix: a licence-back to the customization Deliverables plus a data-use limitation, inserted at the customization clause.","proposal":"Add a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence (use, modify, sublicense) to customization Deliverables we pay for, and limit Licensor's rights in our data to processing to provide the services.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-lol-cap-fcfec618","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION","rationale":"Article XIII caps only Licensor's liability, at one half of amounts paid — well below six months' fees — while Licensee's liability (including its broad Article XII indemnity) is entirely uncapped and no carve-outs exist. That is walk-away territory on both counts (one-sided cap; Vendor cap below 6 months' fees; indemnities inside/outside asymmetry). We target the fallback: a mutual cap based on 12 months' fees with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct. We have not disturbed the one-sided consequential-damages exclusion in clause (a) or clause (c), which fall outside the fallback checklist but remain noted for negotiation.","proposal":"Make the liability cap mutual, set it at 12 months' fees, and place indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct outside the cap.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-d6b135ce","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"GENERAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"Two walk-away features: (i) Article XXIV(c) imposes a blanket prohibition on any Licensee assignment with no affiliate or M&A carve-out (and no reciprocal restriction on Licensor, who may assign freely, including to our competitors), and (ii) Article XX(a) makes any Change of Control of Licensee an automatic termination of the Agreement and of all our licences, subject only to Licensor's consent, which Licensor is deemed reasonable in withholding on broad self-interest grounds. This fails the fallback (no mutual successor-assignment right) and is expressly walk-away territory. We therefore move to the preferred position: affiliate and successor assignment without consent for Licensee, Licensor assignment only with our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a Licensee competitor, and no Licensor termination right on our Change of Control. Consent remains required for other Licensee assignments, and the Change of Control definition is retained for the amended Article XX(a).","proposal":"Add Licensee affiliate/successor assignment rights, restrict Licensor assignment, and remove automatic termination on Licensee Change of Control.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-exclusivity-bd5d4b25","ruleId":"EXCLUSIVITY","ruleTitle":"Exclusivity obligations binding Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us, so it sits at the preferred position. The licence is expressly non-exclusive (Articles II and IV, and the recitals), and nothing requires us to source all or any of our Spot FX platform, liquidity or related services from Licensor or bars us from procuring from third parties. Two nearby provisions were checked and are not exclusivity: (i) the \"Field of Use\" definition and Article II restrictions limit how we may use Licensor's own Licensed Technology (a licence-scope/field-of-use restraint on Licensor's IP, not a requirements or sole-source commitment on us); and (ii) the Article XXII \"Right of First Refusal\" is a first-refusal right over a third-party offer to buy our assets or merge with us — a change-of-control mechanic (and we expressly \"shall have the right to consummate the transaction with the third party\" if it is not exercised), not a restraint on buying competing services. The non-exclusivity language in p0043 confirming Licensor may license others operates in Licensor's favour and is not a deviation under this rule. No fallback narrowing (category, 12-month cap, SLA/delivery-date exit) is needed because there is no exclusivity to narrow.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-a0525f00","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION","rationale":"The Agreement imposes no liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination/minimum fee on us. Article XXIII (p0142) expressly provides that neither party is liable for damages of any kind on account of termination or expiration, and Article XXI's effect-of-termination provision (p0138) requires only return of Licensed Technology, with no exit payment. The payment mechanics we checked are ordinary consideration, not liquidated amounts: the volume-band user fees and the accrual floor tied to actual recorded trading (p0070), the $2,500 monthly support fee, the audit-cost shift if a discrepancy over 5% is found (p0064), and Licensor's retained right on immediate termination to receive payments \"for all trades performed using the Licensed Technology\" (p0049) — i.e., fees already earned, not accelerated or unearned remaining contract value. This meets the preferred position (Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties), so no redline is proposed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-68d3374b","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:","rationale":"The Article II grant (p0030) runs to Licensee alone, and the restrictions confine access to \"employees of the Licensee\" (p0045), so our Affiliates have no coverage and no notice-based path to it. On transferability, Licensee may not assign or transfer its licence rights without consent (p0149), and any merger, asset sale or change of control automatically terminates the Agreement and all licences unless Licensor consents in advance (p0134) - consent deemed reasonably withheld on broad grounds. The clause therefore fails both fallback elements (affiliates on written notice; transfer to an M&A successor), so we made the shortest fallback-level edits: affiliates on written notice in the grant, a conforming change to the employee-access restriction, and a successor-transfer carve-out from the Change of Control auto-termination. We have not pursued the preferred perpetual/irrevocable or contractor elements.","proposal":"Extend the licence to Licensee's Affiliates on written notice and permit transfer of the licence to a successor in a merger or acquisition.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-noncompete-84edd757","ruleId":"NONCOMPETE","ruleTitle":"Non-compete restrictions on Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ I CERTAIN DEFINITIONS For the purposes of this Agreement:","rationale":"No provision restrains the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build, so the rule sits at the preferred position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer). The only \"field of use\" language (1.5, and the grant at p0030 \"solely in the Field of Use\", plus the use limits at p0033 and the Article II Additional Restrictions) limits how we may use Licensor's own Licensed Technology — a licence-scope term rather than a restraint on our FX business; the licence is expressly non-exclusive (p0043), and nothing prevents us from using, licensing, developing or acquiring alternative platforms or products. Article X contains only a non-solicitation of Licensor's employees (p0125), not a non-compete. The Change of Control consent/termination mechanic (p0134) and the Right of First Refusal (Article XXII) constrain a sale of our company rather than our operating business; those sit under the assignment/change-of-control rule and are not flagged twice here. Noted for information only, without redlining: the Field of Use excludes \"any functions or applications not expressly described\", so any future non-Spot FX use of the Platform would need a scope amendment.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-t4c-5d2769e1","ruleId":"T4C","ruleTitle":"Termination for convenience","severity":"high","status":"missing","sectionRef":"§ II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:","rationale":"The Agreement commits Licensee to a 36-month Initial Period, but no provision anywhere permits Licensee to terminate for convenience: the only termination rights are Licensor's immediate termination for Licensee breach (p0049, p0043), mutual insolvency termination (p0132), Change of Control/wind-up termination (p0134, p0137) and effect-of-termination mechanics (p0138). Absence of any Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is walk-away territory under T4C, so we insert the preferred position: Licensee convenience termination on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, plus an express bar on Licensor convenience termination during the term. Licensor's renewal option in Article IV is a renewal issue, not a mid-term Vendor convenience right, and is not flagged here.","proposal":"Add Licensee convenience termination on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and bar Licensor convenience termination during the term.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-052b44a8","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"50+ US$5.00","rationale":"The only audit right binding us (Article IV(b)) is unlimited in frequency: Licensor may demand audits as often as it likes, and the 30-day reference is a deadline for us to permit the audit rather than advance notice, so the clause fails even the fallback (once per year on 15 days' notice) and sits in walk-away territory for unlimited audits. Cost allocation already meets the preferred position (Licensor bears cost unless a discrepancy over 5% is found) and the auditor is already an independent CPA/Audit Professional, so we have taken the preferred level and added only the missing frequency, notice, business-hours, off-site, auditor confidentiality and no-system-access limits.","proposal":"Limit audit frequency and notice and add business-hours, off-site, confidentiality and no-system-access protections","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-govlaw-4ea84ff3","ruleId":"GOVLAW","ruleTitle":"Governing law and venue","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"GENERAL PROVISIONS","rationale":"Governing law is the internal laws of the State of New York (p0145), and disputes must be instituted in the City of New York with irrevocable submission to the exclusive jurisdiction of the SDNY or any New York State court, plus waivers of venue and forum non conveniens objections (p0146). There is no arbitration clause anywhere in the document, so the walk-away risk of an offshore seat does not arise. This sits at the preferred position: New York law and exclusive New York state and federal courts. The only shortfall is cosmetic — venue is fixed to the City of New York rather than New York County specifically, and there is no express temporary-injunctive-relief carve-out (a permitted, not required, feature) — which we note but do not redline.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-mfn-63c9f66f","ruleId":"MFN","ruleTitle":"Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION","rationale":"No pricing MFN exists in the Agreement (Articles V-VIII are only the tiered per-trade fee table, and the Revisions clause at p0094 runs in our favour). Article XXII, however, imposes a most-favoured-offer/right-to-match mechanic on us: we must notify Licensor of any bona fide third-party offer for our assets or a merger and give Licensor five business days to take that offer. The playbook assesses right-to-match and most-favoured-offer mechanics under MFN, and this one fails every fallback element - it is not confined to a defined product, it runs for the whole term (36 months plus a possible seven-year renewal at Licensor's option), and it has no like-for-like comparison carve-out. We therefore take the preferred position: the operative grant is replaced with a one-line no-first-refusal/no-match statement, and the follow-on sentence is restated so it carries its own antecedent for the transaction and the third party and remains expressly subject to the retained Change Of Control (p0134) and Assignment (p0149) consent provisions, so nothing dangles or contradicts.","proposal":"Negate the Article XXII first-refusal/matching mechanic and restate the follow-on sentence with its own antecedent, subordinated to the retained Change of Control and Assignment sections.","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-mincommit-31f4ea47","ruleId":"MINCOMMIT","ruleTitle":"Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:","rationale":"This Agreement sits at the preferred position: there is no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall charge, or volume floor imposed on Licensee anywhere in the payment provisions. Article V fixes user fees solely by reference to actual Monthly Notional Volume traded on the Platform (p0056-p0063), and the monthly calculation in p0070 is expressly based on volume actually traded (\"the amount recorded by the Licensee as being traded with the Licensed Technology multiplied by the applicable Fees\"), so Licensee pays only for usage. The tiered banding in p0067 operates in our favour (the highest band reached applies to all trades that month). The only other recurring charge is $2,500 per month for Technical Support Services actually provided (p0086), which is an ordered service, and p0089 confirms \"Except for the Charges set forth above, there shall be no additional fees payable by the Licensee to the Licensor\". Noted but not flagged: the \"Supplemental Payments\" revenue share (33% of third-party amounts earned from Licensed Technology usage) is an economic term rather than a minimum commitment and applies only \"(if any)\" such amounts are earned; and the 36-month Initial Period is a term length, not a volume commitment, so no exit/true-down mechanic is required under this rule.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-ab0d318a","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION","rationale":"Article X(b) binds only Licensee (one-way), covers every person employed by Licensor and its Affiliates rather than only personnel involved in the services, and runs three years after expiration or termination — well past the 12-month fallback limit. The existing \"Solicit\" definition already excludes general job advertising and responsive/voluntary employment inquiries, and there is no no-hire element, so the failures are mutuality, personnel scope and duration. Our edit makes the restriction mutual, limits it to persons directly involved in the services under this Agreement, and caps it at 12 months after that individual's involvement ends (removing the open-ended \"during the Term\" plus three-year post-termination tail), leaving the favourable carve-out sentence verbatim. The preferred position is no non-solicit on Licensee at all, which we would raise as the opening ask.","proposal":"Narrow one-way three-year non-solicit to mutual, 12 months, involved personnel only","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-renewal-b8bf2ee0","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ II LICENSE GRANT AND RESTRICTIONS I. Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:","rationale":"Article IV (p0049) lets the Licensor unilaterally extend the 36-month Initial Period by a further seven years, with no Licensee opt-out or notice window. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Spot FX Platform Licence Agreement

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Re:** Verified playbook findings and recommended redlines

## Executive summary

We have completed the playbook review of the draft Agreement. Eighteen rules were assessed: five clauses are compliant, ten are deviations requiring redlines, and three rules are unaddressed in the document (termination for convenience, transition assistance and data return, and Vendor insurance).

The risk is concentrated and structurally one-sided in the Licensor's favour. Eight findings sit in walk-away territory: there is no Licensor IP indemnity at all (Article XII is a one-way Licensee indemnity, and Article XIII states that "UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE" for third-party infringement claims); the liability cap is one-sided at one half of amounts paid while our liability is uncapped with no carve-outs; the Licensor may assign freely while we may not, and any Change of Control of Licensee automatically terminates the Agreement and all licences; we are committed to a 36-month Initial Period with no convenience exit, while the Licensor holds a unilateral option to extend by a further seven years; the Licensed Technology is provided "AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed; audits may be demanded without frequency limit or advance notice; and there is no insurance covenant despite the Licensor hosting the Platform and processing our trade data.

Ownership is also adverse: enhancements and customisation work we commission and pay for under Article VII(b) vest in the Licensor as Derivative Works, our licence is non-exclusive, non-modifiable, non-transferable and terminates with the Agreement, and there is no limitation on the Licensor's use of data we supply. Separately, Article XXII imposes a first-refusal/right-to-match mechanic over any third-party offer for our assets or a merger, on five business days' notice.

On the positive side, the Agreement imposes no exclusivity, no non-compete, no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment, and no liquidated damages or early-termination charge on us, and governing law and venue (New York law; exclusive SDNY and New York State courts, with no arbitration clause) sit at our preferred position.

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION (Articles XII–XIII) |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. (Licensee acknowledges and agrees that:) |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION (Article XIII) |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | GENERAL PROVISIONS (Articles XXIV(c), XX(a)) |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § I Certain Definitions |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Deviation | Article IV(b) (fee table, "50+ US$5.00") |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION (Article XXII) |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Deviation | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION (Article X(b)) |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Deviation | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. (Article IV) |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Missing | CONFIDENTIAL INFORMATION/NON SOLICITATION (after Article XXI) |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Deviation | WARRANTY DISCLAIMER (Article VIX) |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § II Licence Grant and Restrictions I. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | GENERAL PROVISIONS |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Missing | GENERAL PROVISIONS |

## Walk-away items

These eight findings fall into walk-away territory under the playbook and must be resolved before signature:

1. **No Vendor IP indemnity (INDEMN).** Article XII is a one-way Licensee indemnity, and Article XIII disclaims all Licensor liability for third-party infringement. We add a Licensor IP indemnity at the fallback level — customary Licensee modification, combination and specification exclusions, procure/modify/replace and refund remedies, and a 3x annual fees super-cap — and conform Article XIII so the indemnity is not negated. We leave the existing Licensee indemnity in place.
2. **One-sided cap below floor (LOL-CAP).** Article XIII caps only the Licensor, at one half of amounts paid (below six months' fees), while our liability, including the broad Article XII indemnity, is uncapped with no carve-outs. We target the fallback: mutual cap at 12 months' fees, with indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct outside the cap. The one-sided consequential-damages exclusion in clause (a) and clause (c) are noted for negotiation but not redlined.
3. **Assignment and Change of Control (ASSIGN).** Article XXIV(c) bars any Licensee assignment with no affiliate or M&A carve-out while the Licensor may assign freely, including to our competitors; Article XX(a) makes any Change of Control of Licensee an automatic termination of the Agreement and all licences. We move to the preferred position: affiliate and successor assignment without consent, Licensor assignment only with our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a competitor, and removal of the Change of Control termination right.
4. **No Customer convenience exit in a 36-month term (T4C).** No provision permits us to terminate for convenience. We insert the preferred position: 30 days' written notice with pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, plus an express bar on Licensor convenience termination during the term.
5. **Unilateral seven-year renewal (RENEWAL).** Article IV lets the Licensor extend the Initial Period by a further seven years with no Licensee opt-out or notice window. We delete the option so renewal requires mutual written agreement.
6. **"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed (WARRANTY).** Article VIX disclaims all warranties and expressly disclaims that nonconformity to Documentation will be corrected; Article VII(f) Error Corrections is not a warranty and carries no remedy. We redline to the fallback: 90-day software conformance warranty, 30-day services warranty, repair/replacement or refund, and an express carve-out from both disclaimer sentences.
7. **Unlimited audit rights (AUDIT).** Article IV(b) permits audits at any frequency, and the 30-day reference is our deadline to permit the audit rather than advance notice. Cost allocation (Licensor bears cost unless a discrepancy over 5% is found) and the independent CPA requirement already meet the preferred position; we add frequency, notice, business-hours, off-site, auditor confidentiality and no-system-access limits.
8. **No insurance covenant (INSURANCE).** The only reference to insurance is a pass-through of charges payable by us. Given the Licensor hosts the Platform and processes our trade data, we insert a covenant at the fallback limits (E&O USD 1M; cyber and privacy USD 2M), and would accept the preferred CGL/E&O USD 2M and cyber USD 5M package.

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the ten deviations and three missing clauses, opening at the positions recorded above. Where we have drafted to the fallback (IP licence-back and data-use limitation; mutual 12-month cap; Licensor IP indemnity; 90/30-day warranties; insurance limits; affiliate and successor licence rights), we should state the fallback on the face of the comment so the Licensor understands the concession already made.
2. **Escalate the eight walk-away items** to the business owner before the next call. Recommended non-negotiables: a Licensor IP indemnity, a mutual cap with carve-outs, a Customer convenience exit, removal of the unilateral seven-year renewal, and deletion of the automatic termination on our Change of Control.
3. **Confirm the two repaired redlines** — MFN (Article XXII first-refusal/matching mechanic, with the follow-on sentence restated to carry its own antecedent and subordinated to the retained Change of Control and Assignment provisions) and NOSOLICIT (Article X(b) narrowed to mutual, 12 months, involved personnel only, retaining the favourable carve-out sentence verbatim) — read cleanly against the retained text before the draft goes out.
4. **Note for the business, without redlining:** the Field of Use excludes any functions or applications not expressly described, so any future non-Spot FX use of the Platform will require a scope amendment; and the Supplemental Payments revenue share (33% of third-party amounts earned from use of the Licensed Technology) is an economic term for commercial review rather than a legal deviation.
5. **Do not reopen the compliant items** (exclusivity, non-compete, minimum commitments, liquidated damages, governing law and venue); they sit at our preferred position and are helpful trading stock in the negotiation."}
